turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: As a psychology professor, I'd say that our brains are quite amazing at filling in the gaps when it comes to speech perception. Even if a sound is intentionally made inaudible, our brains can still recognize the intended word due to the context and the surrounding sounds. This process is known as phoneme restoration, where our brain "hears" the missing sound based on the other sounds in the word. So, in your example, if someone mumbles the middle part of 'strawberry', your brain would still likely recognize it as 'strawberry'. However, consistent errors or unusual pronunciations can make communication more challenging, as our brains may struggle to correctly interpret the intended word.
